correctness.rationale: Exact Kent exponential sum and Rayleigh cumulants yield matching means, variances and explicit nonzero third-cumulant difference. The Bessel Sturm–Liouville min–max bounds imply O(a^{-1/2}) maximal normalized weight and at least floor(a) comparable weights. These prove integrable characteristic-function tail bounds; the Taylor remainder has du/|u| integral O(a^{-1}). Fourier inversion gives uniform signed CDF error O(a^{-1}); the Hermite extremum yields the sharp 1/(3 sqrt(2 pi)) coefficient. Standalone symbolic and numerical checks corroborate constants and sign; they are not infinite-limit proof.

value.rationale: The natural one-factor Gamma approximation in a 2026 first-passage paper lacked a quantified high-dimensional regime. This result proves its exact global CDF error shape and optimal leading Kolmogorov constant, revealing that first-two-moment matching leaves a nonzero skewness-controlled error. The sharp uniform result is useful for choosing approximations in large dimension and is stronger than pointwise skewness or a routine moment comparison.
